key_insight: A wave-particle decomposition rewrites the full Boltzmann collision operator into a wave part plus an exact particle remainder, yielding a closed multiscale system that smoothly bridges Boltzmann and Navier–Stokes regimes.
engineering_relevance: This gives a unified solver for rarefied-to-near-continuum flows that can dramatically reduce iteration counts while retaining kinetic accuracy in challenging aerospace and microflow applications.
method: Transform the collision term into relaxation toward a local Maxwellian plus a conservative remainder.
Define the wave by an equilibrium integral over a local kinetic horizon; define the particle as the exact complement.
Solve coupled wave-particle equations by implicit iteration with macroscopic prediction and endpoint traction coupling.
evidence_signal: The paper reports agreement with benchmark flows (normal shock, Couette, cavity, hypersonic cylinder, Apollo) and shows about 3 to >4 orders of magnitude fewer iterations than conventional iterative schemes near the continuum limit.
watch_item: The method relies on discrete compatibility assumptions and horizon/relaxation scaling, so implementation details may affect stability, fixed-point preservation, and performance.
paper_title: Wave-Particle Decomposition for Kinetic Equations II: Full Boltzmann equation
